topic: Cloze Test (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Cloze Test
sections.content: In a Cloze Test, a short passage is given in which some words are missing. You must choose the correct word for each blank. The correct answer depends on both grammar and context.

sections.title: Articles (a, an, the)
sections.content: Step 1: Look at the noun that comes after the blank. Step 2: If the noun begins with a vowel sound, use 'an'; if it begins with a consonant sound, use 'a'. Step 3: Use 'the' when the noun is specific or already known. Example: He saw a dog in the street.

sections.title: Basic Prepositions
sections.content: Step 1: Identify place, time, or direction in the sentence. Step 2: Choose the correct preposition such as in, on, at, to, or from. Step 3: Select the option that sounds most natural according to the context. Example: She lives in Delhi.

sections.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the subject of the sentence. Step 2: Determine whether the subject is singular or plural. Step 3: Choose the correct form of the verb accordingly. Example: The boy plays cricket.

sections.title: Simple Contextual Vocabulary
sections.content: Step 1: Read the complete sentence carefully. Step 2: Understand the meaning using the words before and after the blank. Step 3: Choose the word that best fits the context. Example: The weather was very cold, so we stayed inside.

sections.title: Basic Conjunctions
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the relationship between the two clauses. Step 2: Use 'and' if the ideas are being added. Step 3: Use 'but' if there is a contrast. Step 4: Use 'so' if the second clause shows a result. Example: He was tired, so he slept early.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing an answer without reading the entire passage. 2. Ignoring grammar rules. 3. Selecting an answer by looking at only one word instead of considering the full context.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In a Cloze Test, both grammar and context are important. First understand the sentence, then apply grammar rules, and finally choose the word that best fits the context.

tricks.title: Sentence First Rule
tricks.explanation: Read the entire sentence before filling the blank.
tricks.example: He was hungry, so he ate food.

tricks.title: Grammar Check Trick
tricks.explanation: Look at the words around the blank and apply the grammar rule.

tricks.title: Article Sound Trick
tricks.explanation: Choose 'a' or 'an' based on the sound of the noun.

tricks.title: Subject Verb Quick Check
tricks.explanation: If the subject is singular, use a singular verb.

tricks.title: Context Guess Method
tricks.explanation: Guess the correct word based on the meaning of the sentence.
tricks.example: It was raining, so we stayed home.

tricks.title: Elimination Trick
tricks.explanation: Remove options that are grammatically or contextually incorrect.
tricks.example: If an article is needed, eliminate verb options.
